text:
Rasmus Andersson came to Vegas from Calgary last season after nearly 600 games as a Flame, and his first full fall in the desert has been quiet. Seven points in 21 games, none on the power play, and two in his last ten, though one of them was a wrister from the slot against Juuse Saros on Friday.

Most of the shortfall is luck. Vegas has scored about nine fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, one of the worst marks on the team, and that usually swings back. His own goals are fine (three on 2.3 expected). The less flattering number is the play itself: the Golden Knights take 48% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him out there, six and a half points worse than without him.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.7 wins last season, 34th among 215 defensemen, mostly from even-strength offense, so the points have a history of coming. He leads the team's defense with 35 blocked shots. With the bounces due to even out, the open question is whether the five-on-five play follows them.
